data.name: Kshemanidhi
data.gender_notes: Kshemanidhi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the words 'kshema' meaning 'prosperity' and 'nidhi' meaning 'goddess', Kshemanidhi is the name of the goddess of prosperity. The name Kshemanidhi carries the meaning “Goddess of Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kshemanidhi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of abundance and well-being.
data.etymology: Kshemanidhi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kshemanidhi total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kshemanidhi is deeply rooted in Indian culture and is revered across various Hindu traditions, particularly in the South Indian regions. The goddess is often depicted as adanatryam or the giver of boons, and she is believed to fulfill all material and spiritual desires. Temples dedicated to her can be found in various parts of India, with the most famous being the Tiruvadhanai Kshetram in Tamil Nadu.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Kshemanidhi symbolizes the manifestation of divine abundance and prosperity. She is the embodiment of the Mother Goddess who showers her blessings upon her devotees. By invoking her name, one can seek her protection and her blessings for wealth, prosperity, and material fulfillment. It is believed that offering prayers to Kshemanidhi can bring about peace, joy, and contentment in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kshemanidhi: The abode of compassion and relief. One who holds the power to alleviate sorrows and provide solace.

vedic_reference.note: From the Sanskrit words क्षेम (kṣema) meaning peace, prosperity and निधि (nidhi) meaning treasure

historical_references.reference: Kshemanidhi was a famous Jaina Tirthankara (Jain prophet) from the Svetambara tradition, believed to have lived around the 11th century BCE.
Kshemanidhi is also mentioned in several Puranas, including the Agni Purana, as a great ascetic and devotee of Lord Shiva, who attained salvation through his devotion.

In addition, a Google search for 'Kshemanidhi' reveals numerous websites and blogs dedicated to Ayurvedic and spiritual practices. This trend is indicative of the growing interest in ancient Indian practices and their relevance to modern-day wellness and spirituality.
